1. K is the reflection of H in BC, so BC is the perpendicular bisector of HK; hence BC ⟂ HK. (1)

2. AH ⟂ BC and HK ⟂ BC, so A, H, K are collinear. (2)

3. We show that A, B, C, K lie on one circle:

∠C = 90° − ∠HBC    [BH ⟂ AC]
   = ∠BHK    [BC ⟂ HK, by (1)]
   = ∠HKB    [BH = BK]
   = ∠AKB    [A, H, K collinear, by (2); H lies on the segment KA]

∠C = ∠AKB and C, K lie on the same side of AB, so by the converse of the inscribed angle theorem, A, B, C, K lie on one circle, as required. ∎
